name: Alternator Replacement — 2015 Honda Civic
safetyWarnings: Disconnect negative battery terminal before starting
Engine may be hot — wait 30 minutes after use
Use jack stands if working underneath

steps.title: Safety Preparation
steps.action: Disconnect the negative battery terminal
steps.visualCues: Black cable, minus sign, 10mm nut on battery
steps.safetyWarning: Prevents short circuits when removing the alternator
commonMistakes: Forgetting to disconnect
Touching both terminals simultaneously

steps.title: Access
steps.action: Remove the engine cover if present
steps.visualCues: Plastic clips on the sides — pull up firmly
commonMistakes: Breaking clips by pulling in the wrong direction

steps.title: Electrical Disconnect
steps.action: Unplug the alternator harness connector
steps.visualCues: Push the tab on top, then pull straight out
commonMistakes: Breaking the tab — use a flathead if stuck

steps.title: Remove Belt
steps.action: Loosen the tensioner and slip the belt off the alternator pulley
steps.visualCues: 14mm bolt on the tensioner arm — rotate clockwise to release
steps.safetyWarning: Engine may be hot — wear gloves
commonMistakes: Forgetting to photograph belt routing before removal

steps.title: Mounting Bolts
steps.action: Remove the top and bottom 12mm mounting bolts
steps.visualCues: Top bolt near windshield, bottom bolt near radiator
steps.torqueSpec: 47 Nm for both bolts on reassembly
commonMistakes: Dropping bolts into the engine bay — use a magnetic tray

steps.title: Remove Alternator
steps.action: Work the alternator out of its bracket
steps.visualCues: May need to tilt — watch for coolant lines nearby

steps.title: Installation
steps.action: Reverse steps 6 through 1
steps.safetyWarning: Torque bolts to spec — do not overtighten
commonMistakes: Overtightening bolts and stripping threads

name: Brake Pad Replacement — Generic Front Disc
safetyWarnings: Never work under a car supported only by a floor jack — use jack stands
Brake dust is hazardous — do not blow with compressed air
Pump brake pedal before driving to seat the pads

steps.title: Loosen Lug Nuts
steps.action: Break lug nuts loose while the wheel is still on the ground
steps.visualCues: Turn counterclockwise — do not remove yet

steps.title: Jack Up and Support
steps.action: Raise the vehicle and place jack stands under the frame
steps.safetyWarning: Never skip the jack stands
commonMistakes: Placing jack stands on body panels instead of frame rails

steps.title: Remove Wheel
steps.action: Remove lug nuts and pull wheel off
steps.visualCues: Set wheel flat as a backup in case jack stands fail

steps.title: Remove Caliper
steps.action: Remove the two caliper slide bolts (usually 12mm) and slide the caliper off
steps.visualCues: Bolts are on the back side of the caliper
steps.safetyWarning: Do not let the caliper hang by the brake hose — hang it with a wire hook
commonMistakes: Letting the caliper stretch or kink the brake line

steps.title: Remove Old Pads
steps.action: Slide old pads out of the caliper bracket
steps.visualCues: Note orientation — outer pad has the wear indicator clip

steps.title: Compress Piston
steps.action: Use a C-clamp to press the caliper piston back in
steps.visualCues: Use the old pad as a buffer between clamp and piston
steps.safetyWarning: Watch brake fluid reservoir — may overflow; remove some if needed

steps.title: Install New Pads
steps.action: Slide new pads into the caliper bracket, apply caliper grease to tabs
steps.visualCues: Anti-squeal shims face outward
commonMistakes: Forgetting to lubricate slide pins — causes uneven wear

steps.title: Reassemble and Test
steps.action: Reinstall caliper, torque slide bolts, mount wheel
steps.safetyWarning: Pump brake pedal 10 times before moving the car

name: Electrolytic Capacitor Replacement
safetyWarnings: Discharge capacitors before touching — measure with multimeter first
Electrolytic capacitors are polarised — match stripe (negative) to PCB marking
Keep iron tip temperature under 380°C to avoid PCB damage
Work in a ventilated area — solder fumes are harmful

steps.title: Power Off and Discharge
steps.action: Unplug the device and measure capacitor voltage with a multimeter
steps.visualCues: Probe across cap legs — wait for reading to drop below 1V
steps.safetyWarning: Large caps in amplifiers can hold lethal charge for hours

steps.title: ESD Setup
steps.action: Attach ESD wrist strap to your wrist and clip to ground
steps.visualCues: Metal chassis screw or bare copper are good ground points

steps.title: Identify Polarity
steps.action: Note the negative stripe on the capacitor and the PCB half-moon marking
steps.visualCues: Light-coloured stripe = negative lead; half-moon on PCB = negative hole
commonMistakes: Reversing polarity — capacitor will fail or explode under power

steps.title: Desolder Old Capacitor
steps.action: Heat each leg and remove solder with desoldering pump
steps.visualCues: Apply fresh solder first if old solder won't flow — it helps
commonMistakes: Overheating the pad — lift PCB trace

steps.title: Clean Holes
steps.action: Clear holes with desoldering braid, confirm clean with a pin
steps.visualCues: Holes should be fully open and shiny

steps.title: Insert New Capacitor
steps.action: Insert new cap with correct polarity, bend legs slightly to hold
steps.visualCues: Stripe faces the half-moon PCB marking

steps.title: Solder and Trim
steps.action: Solder both legs, trim excess lead with flush cutters
steps.visualCues: Good joint is shiny and volcano-shaped, not dull or balled
commonMistakes: Cold solder joints — reheat and add a tiny amount of flux

steps.title: Verify
steps.action: Power on and check voltage across capacitor terminals with multimeter
steps.visualCues: Should match the capacitor's rated working voltage for the circuit

name: Washing Machine Pump Filter Cleaning
safetyWarnings: Unplug machine from the wall before any work — water and electricity are fatal
Shut off water supply valves behind the machine
Have towels ready — filter housing holds up to 1 litre of water

steps.title: Unplug and Isolate
steps.action: Unplug the washing machine from the power outlet
steps.visualCues: Reach behind — the outlet is usually above the machine
steps.safetyWarning: Do not skip this step

steps.title: Locate Access Panel
steps.action: Find the circular access panel on the lower front right of the machine
steps.visualCues: Small rectangular or square panel near the floor

steps.title: Open Access Panel
steps.action: Pry open the panel using a flathead or press the clips
steps.visualCues: Panel hinges or comes away completely

steps.title: Drain Residual Water
steps.action: Place tray under filter — pull the small rubber drain hose and uncap it
steps.visualCues: Small black or grey hose tucked next to the filter cap
commonMistakes: Unscrewing filter before draining — floods the floor

steps.title: Remove Filter
steps.action: Turn filter cap counterclockwise and pull out
steps.visualCues: Counter-clockwise to loosen — may be stiff on first removal

steps.title: Clean Filter
steps.action: Remove debris, rinse under hot water, check rubber seal
steps.visualCues: Look for coins, hair, small garments — common blockages
commonMistakes: Reinstalling without replacing damaged O-ring — causes leaks

steps.title: Reinstall and Test
steps.action: Screw filter back in hand-tight, recap drain hose, close panel
steps.safetyWarning: Do not overtighten filter — thread is plastic
commonMistakes: Forgetting to recap the drain hose before running a cycle

name: AC Contactor Replacement
safetyWarnings: Turn off the breaker AND verify with a multimeter before opening the unit
Capacitors hold dangerous charge — discharge with insulated resistor before touching
Only a licensed technician may handle refrigerant — do not open refrigerant lines
Wear rubber-soled shoes when working near the outdoor unit

steps.title: Kill Power
steps.action: Turn off the AC breaker in your electrical panel
steps.visualCues: Usually a double-pole 30–60A breaker labelled AC or HVAC

steps.title: Disconnect Service Disconnect
steps.action: Pull out or flip the outdoor service disconnect near the unit
steps.visualCues: Metal box on the wall next to the outdoor condenser

steps.title: Verify No Voltage
steps.action: Open the service panel on the condenser and test for voltage with multimeter
steps.visualCues: Probe the two large line-voltage wires — reading must be 0V
steps.safetyWarning: Do not proceed if you see any voltage reading

steps.title: Discharge Capacitor
steps.action: Discharge the run capacitor using an insulated 10kΩ resistor across each pair of terminals
steps.visualCues: Capacitor is the silver or black cylinder with wires on top
steps.safetyWarning: Never short the capacitor directly — can cause serious burns

steps.title: Photograph Wiring
steps.action: Take a clear photo of the contactor wiring before disconnecting anything
commonMistakes: Skipping the photo and being unable to reconnect correctly

steps.title: Remove Old Contactor
steps.action: Unscrew the two line-voltage wires from the top terminals and the low-voltage wires from the coil
steps.visualCues: Line voltage (thick wires) at top, 24V coil wires (thin, usually red/yellow) at the side

steps.title: Mount New Contactor
steps.action: Screw new contactor into the same mounting position
commonMistakes: Buying wrong amp rating — must match old unit (20A, 30A, or 40A)

steps.title: Reconnect Wires
steps.action: Reconnect wires using your photo as reference — line voltage to top, coil to side
steps.safetyWarning: Ensure no bare wire is exposed outside its terminal

steps.title: Test
steps.action: Replace service panel cover, restore power, set thermostat to cooling
steps.visualCues: You should hear the contactor click and the compressor start within 5 minutes

name: Spark Plug Replacement — Mazda CX-9
safetyWarnings: Engine must be cool before starting — hot engine can damage threads
Disconnect battery to prevent accidental engine cranking
Do not drop tools or debris into spark plug holes — can damage cylinders
Always torque spark plugs to spec — overtightening strips threads, undertightening causes blowout

steps.title: Safety Preparation
steps.action: Ensure engine is cool (sitting for at least 2 hours), disconnect negative battery terminal
steps.visualCues: Black cable with minus symbol near battery — 10mm nut
steps.safetyWarning: Prevents accidental cranking and electrical shorts

steps.title: Access Engine Cover
steps.action: Remove plastic engine cover if equipped
steps.visualCues: Four plastic clips or two 10mm bolts on top of engine cover — lift straight up

steps.title: Locate Front Bank Ignition Coils
steps.action: Identify the three ignition coils on the front bank (closest to radiator)
steps.visualCues: Three black plastic rectangles with wiring connectors on top, sitting on valve cover

steps.title: Remove Front Coil Connectors
steps.action: Unplug the wiring connectors from the front three coils
steps.visualCues: Press the release tab and pull connector straight up — do not pull on wires

steps.title: Remove Front Coils
steps.action: Remove the 8mm bolt holding each coil, then pull the coil straight up
steps.visualCues: Small bolt on side of each coil — coil slides into spark plug tube
commonMistakes: Twisting or bending the coil — pull straight to avoid breaking the boot

steps.title: Clean Spark Plug Wells (Front)
steps.action: Blow out any debris from the spark plug wells using compressed air or vacuum
steps.visualCues: Ensure no dirt falls into the cylinder when removing plugs
steps.safetyWarning: Debris in combustion chamber can cause engine damage

steps.title: Remove Front Spark Plugs
steps.action: Use 14mm spark plug socket with extension to loosen and remove plugs
steps.visualCues: Socket fits over the ceramic insulator — turn counterclockwise
commonMistakes: Using a standard socket — spark plug sockets have rubber insert to grip plug

steps.title: Prepare New Plugs (Front)
steps.action: Check gap on new plugs, apply thin coat of anti-seize to threads
steps.visualCues: Gap should be 1.0–1.1mm for CX-9 — use feeler gauge or gap tool
commonMistakes: Getting anti-seize on the electrode — causes misfire

steps.title: Install Front Spark Plugs
steps.action: Thread new plugs by hand first, then torque to 18 Nm (13 lb-ft)
steps.visualCues: Finger-tight until seated, then use torque wrench — do not overtighten
steps.torqueSpec: 18 Nm (13 lb-ft) — do not exceed 20 Nm
steps.safetyWarning: Overtightening strips aluminum threads in cylinder head

steps.title: Reinstall Front Coils
steps.action: Apply dielectric grease to coil boots, push coils onto plugs, reinstall 8mm bolts
steps.visualCues: Small amount of grease on the rubber boot — ensures good connection and prevents arcing

steps.title: Access Rear Bank
steps.action: Remove any intake plumbing blocking access to rear bank
steps.visualCues: May need to remove intake snorkel, PCV hose, or other components — photo connections first

steps.title: Locate Rear Bank Ignition Coils
steps.action: Identify the three ignition coils on the rear bank (closest to firewall)
steps.visualCues: Tucked behind intake manifold — tighter space, may need swivel joint on ratchet

steps.title: Remove Rear Coil Connectors
steps.action: Unplug wiring connectors from rear three coils
steps.visualCues: Same release tab as front — reach carefully, use extension if needed for leverage

steps.title: Remove Rear Coils
steps.action: Remove 8mm bolts and pull coils straight up
steps.visualCues: More limited space — use magnetic pickup tool if bolts are dropped
commonMistakes: Dropping bolts into engine bay — use magnetic tray or tape socket

steps.title: Clean Spark Plug Wells (Rear)
steps.action: Blow out debris from rear wells before removing plugs
steps.visualCues: Compressed air or vacuum — debris more likely to accumulate in rear

steps.title: Remove Rear Spark Plugs
steps.action: Use 14mm socket with long extension and swivel joint
steps.visualCues: Swivel joint helps with angle — be gentle to avoid breaking ceramic
commonMistakes: Forcing socket at wrong angle — can crack plug insulator

steps.title: Install Rear Spark Plugs
steps.action: Thread by hand, then torque to 18 Nm
steps.visualCues: Same process as front — start by hand to avoid cross-threading
steps.safetyWarning: Cross-threading in aluminum head is expensive to repair

steps.title: Reinstall Rear Coils
steps.action: Apply dielectric grease, push coils onto plugs, reinstall bolts
steps.visualCues: Ensure coils seat fully onto plug before tightening bolt

steps.title: Reconnect All Coil Connectors
steps.action: Reconnect all six coil wiring connectors — front and rear
steps.visualCues: Should click firmly into place — tug gently to confirm

steps.title: Reinstall Engine Cover and Intake
steps.action: Replace any removed intake components and engine cover
steps.visualCues: Ensure all hoses and connectors are reattached

steps.title: Reconnect Battery
steps.action: Reconnect negative battery terminal, tighten 10mm nut
steps.visualCues: Terminal should be snug — do not overtighten

steps.title: Test Engine
steps.action: Start engine and verify smooth idle
steps.visualCues: Listen for misfires or rough idle — check engine light should stay off
steps.safetyWarning: If check engine light flashes, shut off immediately — indicates misfire

name: Smartphone Cracked Screen Replacement
safetyWarnings: Always disconnect the battery first — live circuits can short during repair
Lithium batteries can catch fire if punctured — handle with extreme care
Broken glass can cut — wear cut-resistant gloves and eye protection
Do not overheat — keep heat gun/hairdryer under 80°C to avoid damaging components
Work in a low-static environment — ESD can destroy sensitive chips
Document screw locations — mixing them up can damage the logic board

steps.title: Power Off and Prepare
steps.action: Power off the device completely and remove SIM tray
steps.visualCues: Use SIM eject tool to pop out tray from side — keep SIM card safe
steps.safetyWarning: Device must be fully powered down before opening

steps.title: Heat the Screen Edges
steps.action: Apply heat around the screen perimeter to soften adhesive
steps.visualCues: Heat gun at 60–80°C or hairdryer on high — move in circular motion for 2–3 minutes
steps.safetyWarning: Do not focus heat on one spot — can damage OLED panel or battery
commonMistakes: Overheating — causes display discoloration or battery damage

steps.title: Attach Suction Cup
steps.action: Place suction cup near bottom edge of screen
steps.visualCues: Press firmly to create vacuum seal — avoid cracked areas that may shatter
commonMistakes: Placing over deep cracks — suction won't hold and can worsen damage

steps.title: Create Initial Gap
steps.action: Pull suction cup gently while inserting prying tool at seam
steps.visualCues: Screen should lift slightly — insert plastic pick or spudger into the gap
commonMistakes: Using metal tools — will scratch or dent frame
Prying against internal components

steps.title: Separate Adhesive
steps.action: Slide opening tool around perimeter to cut adhesive
steps.visualCues: Keep tool at shallow angle — slide slowly along edges, reheating if resistance is felt
steps.safetyWarning: Cables at top — do not insert tool more than 3mm near top edge
commonMistakes: Cutting flex cables — stop near top where display and digitizer cables are

steps.title: Open Like Book
steps.action: Lift screen from bottom like a book hinge at top
steps.visualCues: Screen should pivot on top edge — display cables connect there
steps.safetyWarning: Do not fully detach yet — flex cables still connected at top

steps.title: Remove Battery Connector Cover
steps.action: Locate and remove metal bracket covering battery connector
steps.visualCues: Small metal plate held by tiny screws — usually near bottom of opened screen
commonMistakes: Skipping this step — working on live circuit risks shorts

steps.title: Disconnect Battery
steps.action: Use spudger to lift battery connector straight up off board
steps.visualCues: Connector pops straight up — do not pry against nearby components
steps.safetyWarning: CRITICAL: This must be done before touching any other connectors — prevents shorts
commonMistakes: Lifting at angle — can bend connector pins

steps.title: Disconnect Screen Cables
steps.action: Disconnect display and digitizer flex cables from logic board
steps.visualCues: Usually 2–3 connectors at top — use spudger to lift retaining brackets first
commonMistakes: Forgetting to flip up retaining brackets — forcing connectors damages pins

steps.title: Remove Old Screen
steps.action: Detach screen assembly completely and set aside
steps.visualCues: Screen is now free — place cracked screen face-down on padded surface
steps.safetyWarning: Handle cracked glass carefully — sharp edges can cut
commonMistakes: Forgetting to transfer components like earpiece speaker, front camera, or home button to new screen

steps.title: Transfer Components (if needed)
steps.action: Remove and transfer earpiece speaker, front camera, sensors, and home button to new screen
steps.visualCues: Small screws hold brackets — use tweezers for tiny flex cables
commonMistakes: Losing tiny screws — use magnetic organizer
Tearing delicate flex cables — work slowly

steps.title: Prepare New Screen
steps.action: Remove protective film and check new screen for damage
steps.visualCues: Inspect for cracks, dead pixels, or digitizer issues before installation

steps.title: Apply New Adhesive
steps.action: Apply fresh adhesive strips around screen frame perimeter
steps.visualCues: Peel backing from adhesive strips — align carefully with frame edges
commonMistakes: Using old adhesive — won't seal properly
Adhesive blocking connectors or screw holes

steps.title: Connect New Screen Cables
steps.action: Attach display and digitizer flex cables to logic board
steps.visualCues: Align connectors carefully — press down until they snap into place, then flip down retaining brackets

steps.title: Reconnect Battery
steps.action: Reconnect battery flex cable to logic board
steps.visualCues: Press connector straight down — should click into place
steps.safetyWarning: Ensure connector is fully seated before reinstalling bracket

steps.title: Install Battery Bracket
steps.action: Reinstall metal cover over battery connector
steps.visualCues: Align screw holes — install screws in same positions (may be different sizes)

steps.title: Test Before Sealing
steps.action: Power on device to verify screen functions correctly
steps.visualCues: Check touch response, display quality, brightness, front camera, earpiece speaker
commonMistakes: Sealing before testing — if defective, must reopen

steps.title: Seal Screen Assembly
steps.action: Press screen firmly into frame to set adhesive
steps.visualCues: Apply even pressure around perimeter — hold for 30 seconds, then place heavy book on top for 30 minutes
steps.safetyWarning: Do not apply pressure to center of screen — can crack display

steps.title: Reinstall Screws
steps.action: Replace bottom pentalobe or screws holding screen
steps.visualCues: Insert SIM tray first, then install screws at bottom or around frame

steps.title: Final Testing
steps.action: Verify all functions work correctly
steps.visualCues: Test: touch sensitivity, display brightness/colors, Face ID/Touch ID, front camera, earpiece, proximity sensor, auto-rotate
commonMistakes: Not testing all features — some sensors may not reconnect properly
